0.3.title: Identity, workspace and data isolation
0.3.parallelNote: This checkout (local branch wip-0.3) contains 0.1, 0.2 (UI platform) and 0.4 (platform services) merged together; 0.4's PR is in CI right now and may receive small fixes that will be merged into your branch later, so do not rework 0.4's files beyond what auth needs. Use 0.4's pieces rather than writing new ones: logger (src/lib/observability), typed errors and withApiErrorHandling (src/lib/errors), rate limiting (src/lib/security/rate-limit.ts, src/lib/rate-limit/, src/middleware.ts), RequestContext (src/app-layer/types.ts), startup checks (src/lib/startup-checks.ts), env modules. npm may skip install scripts: run npm run db:generate after schema changes.
0.3.brief:
Roadmap prompt (docs/ROADMAP.md, Phase 0.3):
Add authentication and tenancy. Lift next-auth 4 configuration from inflect-compliance/src/auth.ts keeping only Credentials (bcrypt, breached-password check, progressive lockout) and Google; drop SAML, OIDC, Entra, SCIM, MFA policy and API keys. Models: User, Workspace, WorkspaceMembership (OWNER, EDITOR, READER), UserSession. Lift the row-level-security pattern from src/lib/db/rls-middleware.ts: every workspace-scoped table has workspaceId, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and is reached through runInWorkspaceContext. Lift field encryption (encryption-middleware, encrypted-fields manifest, per-workspace data key) with an empty manifest to be filled in Phase 1. A new sign-up creates a workspace with its owner. Tests: a two-workspace integration test proving one cannot read the other's rows through the app role, and a guard test that fails when a workspace-scoped model has no RLS policy.

Additional items:
1. Prisma schema files: prisma/schema/enums.prisma (WorkspaceRole and any others), auth.prisma (User, Account, VerificationToken, UserSession, PasswordResetToken if password reset is lifted), workspace.prisma (Workspace with encryptedDek / previousEncryptedDek, WorkspaceMembership). Migrations in prisma/migrations created with prisma migrate (never db push), carrying the RLS SQL the way inflect-compliance does it: an app_user role, a workspace_isolation policy per workspace-scoped table (USING and WITH CHECK), the superuser_bypass policy, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The runtime Prisma client must actually run tenant-scoped queries as app_user (SET LOCAL ROLE + set_config('app.workspace_id') per transaction, as inflect does), and the tripwire that flags a workspace-scoped query outside a context should be lifted. CI's Test job already applies migrations; make sure it still passes.
2. URL shape (owner decision D4 allows an author to belong to more than one workspace later, e.g. as an invited editor): move the app area under /w/[workspaceSlug]/ (books and settings placeholder pages move there; update APP_ROUTES and the palette commands to be built per slug). Workspace API routes live under /api/w/[workspaceSlug]/... (0.4's read rate-limit tier already keys on that segment). / for a signed-in user redirects to their first workspace; signed out, it shows the existing landing page with Sign in / Sign up links.
3. Middleware (src/middleware.ts, extending 0.4's): /w/:slug/** and /api/w/:slug/** require the slug to be in the JWT's memberships[] (cap the claim at 50 like inflect, with a truncated flag that defers to the DB-backed server gate). Mismatch -> redirect /no-workspace (pages) or 403 (API).
4. getWorkspaceCtx(req or params) builds the full RequestContext (requestId, userId, workspaceId, workspaceSlug, role, permissions) from the session and a DB membership check; it is threaded explicitly into usecases. Fill the RequestContext workspace fields 0.4 left optional (make them required on a WorkspaceRequestContext type rather than loosening the base type).
5. Permissions: a small PermissionSet for OWNER/EDITOR/READER (src/lib/permissions.ts) and requirePermission() for API routes modelled on inflect-compliance's permission-middleware; a denial writes an AUTHZ_DENIED audit row and returns a generic 403.
6. Audit: an append-only AuditLog (hash-chained per workspace like inflect-compliance's audit writer, simplified: no outbox, no streaming), written by logEvent(ctx, ...) for sign-up, sign-in success and failure, sign-out, membership changes and authorization denials. A DB trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE on AuditLog. Details carry ids and counts, never author text.
7. Pages: sign-up and sign-in (Credentials; Google button only when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are configured), sign-out, /no-workspace, built on the lifted primitives and next-intl strings. Password policy, the HIBP k-anonymity check (fail-open on outage, never in tests — mock it), progressive lockout with timing equalisation (dummy bcrypt verify), the auth rate-limit tier.
8. Session hardening: a UserSession row per sign-in, verified on each JWT pass; a revoked or expired session makes the JWT callback throw so getServerSession returns null (inflect-compliance's SessionRevokedError pattern, not a flag). A settings page section lists the user's sessions and can revoke the others.
9. Replace the 0.2 WorkspaceContext stub (getCurrentWorkspace) with the real provider fed from getWorkspaceCtx in the /w/[workspaceSlug] layout; the exported interface in src/lib/workspace/workspace-context.tsx must not change.
10. Field encryption: DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (master KEK) required in production via startup-checks and the env schema, dev fallback key with a WARN, per-workspace DEK created at sign-up (createWorkspaceWithDek), v2 envelope, the Prisma $extends query extension wired into src/lib/db.ts, an encrypted-fields manifest that is empty except for a test-only model or a unit test proving round trip and that a manifest field is ciphertext at rest. An encrypt->decrypt sentinel at web and worker startup.
11. Env: NEXTAUTH_URL/AUTH_SECRET (required in production), GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET (optional), DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, in src/env.ts, .env.example and startup-checks.
12. Integration tests: two-workspace isolation through the app role (read, update, insert with a foreign workspaceId, all refused), RLS coverage guard over every workspace-scoped table (fails if one lacks FORCE RLS or the policy), sign-up creates workspace+OWNER membership+DEK atomically, lockout progression, session revocation, audit hash chain verifies and the trigger refuses UPDATE/DELETE. A Playwright spec for sign up -> land in the workspace -> sign out -> sign in (run locally with PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1243/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell).

lenses.name: rls-isolation
lenses.focus: Can any path read or write another workspace's rows? Is app_user really the role at runtime for workspace-scoped queries (not the table owner, which bypasses RLS unless FORCE is set)? FORCE RLS on every workspace table, policies correct for SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE (WITH CHECK), the bypass used only where justified (sign-up, auth lookups by email), the tripwire present, the guard test real and able to fail.

lenses.name: auth-flows
lenses.focus: Sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, lockout progression and timing equalisation, HIBP fail-open, session revocation actually signing the session out (throw, not flag), JWT claims and the membership cap, middleware gate for pages and API, open redirects via callbackUrl, CSRF on credential routes, Google provider only when configured, no password or hash ever logged.

lenses.name: encryption-audit
lenses.focus: Per-workspace DEK created at sign-up and wrapped by the KEK, production refuses to start without a proper key, sentinel at startup, the extension encrypts on write and decrypts on read, the audit chain is per workspace and verifiable, the trigger refuses UPDATE/DELETE, audit details carry no author text or credentials.

2.1-core.title: Model seam, structured output and guard (workspace-independent core)
2.1-core.parallelNote: This checkout (local branch wip-2.1) contains 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4. Subphase 0.3 (auth, workspaces, RLS, the RequestContext's workspace fields, field encryption) is being built concurrently elsewhere and Phase 1 has not started, so build ONLY the parts of 2.1 that do not need a workspace: no Prisma model, no migration, no route. Where the brief needs persistence or a workspace (AiCallLog, the per-workspace monthly spend ceiling), define the interface and an in-memory implementation behind it, so the Prisma-backed implementation can be added once 0.3 lands; say so in the implementation note. npm may skip install scripts: run npm run db:generate if needed.
2.1-core.brief:
Roadmap prompt (docs/ROADMAP.md, Phase 2.1), restricted to the workspace-independent core:
Build the model layer. Lift inflect-compliance/src/lib/agentic/tool-runner/client.ts as src/lib/ai/client.ts (clientForRun), the only file that imports @anthropic-ai/sdk, enforced by the lifted ESLint rule (local/anthropic-client-single-seam, already registered with src/lib/ai/client.ts as its exemption); remove residency and workspace branches, keep the messages-only middleware. Lift the guard scanners from inflect-compliance/src/app-layer/ai/guard (normalize, patterns, injection-scanner, egress-scanner, policy, providers/types, providers/compose, providers/patterns-provider) and write a new thin wrapper with no audit coupling. Add callStructured(schema, prompt): a streamed call returning a Zod-validated object, using the API's structured-output feature; fall back to a single forced tool whose input schema is the output. One repair attempt on validation failure, then a typed error. Model tiers in one file: fast (classification, extraction), balanced (question generation), deep (book-level analysis), each overridable by env. Record every call in AiCallLog (purpose, prompt version, model, tokens, cost, duration, outcome; never the text). Per-workspace monthly spend ceiling modelled on inflect's assistant/spend-ceiling.ts, and a global kill switch. Author text goes in fenced data blocks, never in the system prompt.

How to do it here:
1. Use @anthropic-ai/sdk at exactly inflect-compliance's pinned version (1.8.0) and read its type definitions in node_modules to learn how the SDK expresses structured output (output_config / output_format or equivalent) and streaming in that version; also read how inflect's client.ts pins the base URL, logging, tracing and refuses ambient headers. If a claude-api skill is available to you, load it for the current API reference. Do not guess an API shape: if the pinned SDK version has no native structured-output parameter, implement the forced-tool path as the primary and record it.
2. Model ids: claude-haiku-5-5 (fast), claude-sonnet-5-5 (balanced), claude-opus-5-5 (deep), as defaults overridable by env (AI_MODEL_FAST, AI_MODEL_BALANCED, AI_MODEL_DEEP). A capabilities table per model family decides which parameters are sent (inflect's tool-runner/model-capabilities.ts pattern): an unknown model gets only what every model accepts.
3. Prompt assembly: a single function builds the request: system prompt from a versioned template (prompt id + version string), author text only inside fenced, labelled data blocks in the user turn, never interpolated into the system prompt. Every author-text input passes the injection scanner first; a BLOCK verdict refuses the call with a typed error and an INFO/WARN verdict is recorded. Model output passes the egress scanner before it is returned.
4. AiCallRecorder interface with an in-memory implementation now (fields: purpose, promptId, promptVersion, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, costMicroUsd, durationMs, outcome, guardVerdicts; never any text), a price table per model for cost, a SpendCeiling interface (check before a call, charge after) with an in-memory implementation keyed by an opaque scope id, and a global kill switch read from env (AI_DISABLED=1 refuses every call before anything is built).
5. Env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (optional; absent means every call refuses with a typed AiUnavailableError, never a crash), the model overrides, AI_DISABLED, per-call token budget defaults. All in src/env.ts and .env.example. Production startup does NOT require the key (the product can run with AI off).
6. Tests: never call the network. Inject a fake transport (the SDK client accepts a custom fetch) to test: request shape (system has no author text; author text is fenced; tools/structured output parameters per capability row), streaming accumulation, Zod validation success, one repair attempt then typed error, forced-tool fallback, injection BLOCK refusal before any request, egress scan on output, kill switch refusal before any request, spend ceiling refusal and charging, missing key refusal, the single-seam ESLint rule failing on a second import site (RuleTester case or a lint run on a fixture). Port the guard scanners' own tests from inflect-compliance.
7. Docs: implementation note, carve-manifest rows, CLAUDE.md section 'Model layer' (how to make a model call, what never to do), NOTICE unchanged unless you port third-party code.

lenses.name: model-api-correctness
lenses.focus: Does the request the client builds match what the pinned @anthropic-ai/sdk version and the Messages API actually accept (check node_modules type definitions): structured output or forced tool parameters, streaming event handling, stop reasons, token usage fields, error classes, retries? Does the capabilities table avoid sending parameters a model rejects?

lenses.name: prompt-injection-boundary
lenses.focus: Can author text reach the system prompt, escape its fence (a closing fence or tag inside the text), or reach the model unscanned? Is the egress scan applied to every output path, including the repair attempt and the forced-tool path? Do refusals happen before any network request is built?

0.4.title: Platform services and tooling
0.4.parallelNote: This checkout (local branch wip-0.4) starts from an in-progress snapshot of subphase 0.1. Subphase 0.2 (UI platform: packages/ui, src/components, styles, i18n) is being built concurrently in another checkout and will be merged with yours, so change only the files your brief needs and do not reformat or restructure files you do not need to touch. Subphase 0.3 (auth, workspaces, RLS) has NOT been built: do not build authentication; design the services so 0.3 can plug in (for example rate-limit keys that accept an optional userId, a RequestContext type with optional workspace fields). npm may have skipped install scripts: run npm run db:generate if the Prisma client is missing.
0.4.brief:
Roadmap prompt (docs/ROADMAP.md, Phase 0.4):
Lift the generic platform services: pino logger, OpenTelemetry and Sentry initialisation with graceful shutdown; rate limiting (mutation, read and auth tiers); storage providers (S3, local, ClamAV scan); mailer; BullMQ queue.ts and scheduler.ts with the esbuild worker build and an empty executor registry; withApiErrorHandling and the typed error classes. Lift tests/helpers/repo-files.ts and source-blocks.ts, and the generic ESLint rules (anthropic-client-single-seam, no-raw-prompt-logging, no-request-derived-public-url, the focus-indicator rules). Create .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint, typecheck, unit, integration, build, CodeQL, npm audit at moderate and Trivy, and a release workflow. Lift the Astro Starlight docs site with a single help site.

Additional items:
1. CI: extend the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml keeping the job names Lint, Typecheck, Test, Build unchanged, and add jobs Security (npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate plus the secret scan), CodeQL (github/codeql-action, javascript-typescript), and Docker (build the image, Trivy scan CRITICAL,HIGH, ignore-unfixed). Integration tests run in the Test job (or a separate job named Integration) against the postgres service with migrations applied. Pin third-party actions to a major version at least; least-privilege permissions. Add .github/workflows/release.yml (semantic-release on main) only if it runs with GITHUB_TOKEN alone; otherwise skip it and record why. Add a docs-site workflow that builds the Starlight site on PRs touching docs or site and deploys to GitHub Pages only on main and only when Pages is enabled (guard it so a repo without Pages does not fail).
2. Husky pre-commit running the secret-detection script and .secret-patterns lifted from inflect-compliance, plus a unit guard test that scans the git tree with the same patterns.
3. Health endpoints /api/livez (process up) and /api/readyz (database and Redis reachable, with a timeout; 503 when not) beside the existing /api/health.
4. scripts/worker.ts BullMQ worker entry with an empty executor registry and one no-op heartbeat job proving the wiring end to end, plus npm run build:worker and npm run worker.
5. The logger never logs request bodies; a redaction list covers authorization headers, cookies, passwords, tokens and any field named text, answer, content or body (author text, rule 4 of the roadmap).
6. Rate-limit storage falls back to in-memory when Upstash is not configured; no module-scope setInterval (sweep lazily, as inflect-compliance does).
7. Every new env variable goes in src/env.ts (or env-client.ts) and .env.example in the same change, optional with safe dev defaults; production refuses to start when a required one is missing.
8. The docs site lives under site/ with a single help site whose content comes from docs/user/ (create docs/user/index.md with a one-page 'What Inkquisitor is'); do not publish the roadmap or internal docs.

lenses.name: ci-on-github
lenses.focus: Will every job in the workflows pass on a fresh GitHub runner with only GITHUB_TOKEN: npm ci, Prisma generate, migrations against the service, CodeQL init/analyze, Docker build context and Dockerfile correctness, Trivy step, Pages guard, action versions, permissions blocks. Job names Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build unchanged.

lenses.name: ops-wiring
lenses.focus: Logger/OTel/Sentry initialisation order and no-ops when unconfigured, graceful shutdown on SIGTERM, rate-limit tiers really applied by withApiErrorHandling to mutations, storage and mailer safe defaults in dev, worker boots and processes the heartbeat, readyz really checks DB and Redis with timeouts.

0.2.parallelNote: This checkout (local branch wip-0.2) starts from an in-progress snapshot of subphase 0.1. Subphase 0.4 (platform services, CI) is being built concurrently in another checkout and will be merged with yours, so change only the files your brief needs and do not reformat or restructure files you do not need to touch. 0.2.brief:
Roadmap prompt (docs/ROADMAP.md, Phase 0.2):
Lift the UI platform from inflect-compliance: packages/ui as a workspace package renamed @inkquisitor/ui; the generic primitives in src/components/ui (table, filter, modal, sheet, combobox, form-field, tooltip, date-picker, accordion, radio-group, toggle-group, undo-toast, RichTextEditor, VersionDiff, hooks); the command palette shell; the layout shells in src/components/layout; src/styles/tokens.css, the Tailwind config and ThemeProvider. Leave out FrameworkBuilder, ComplianceStatusIndicator, EvidenceGallery, SankeyChart, GraphExplorer and every domain chart. Replace tenant/org context with a single WorkspaceContext. Rebrand the palette tokens (ink black, parchment, one accent) in light and dark. Build a /dev/kitchen-sink page rendering every primitive, and a rendered test per primitive that it mounts. Record every file in the carve manifest.

Additional items:
1. packages/ui becomes a workspace package @inkquisitor/ui (root package.json workspaces ["packages/*"], tsconfig path @inkquisitor/ui/* the way inflect maps @inflect/ui/*). Rename every @inflect/ui import.
2. Port the primitives' own tests from inflect-compliance (tests/rendered and packages/ui tests where they exist), adapted; add a jest 'rendered' project (jsdom) and make npm test run it alongside unit.
3. i18n: lift the next-intl setup (src/i18n.ts, locale constants, cookie-based locale) with messages/en.json holding only the strings the lifted components use. English only.
4. WorkspaceContext lives at src/lib/workspace/workspace-context.tsx with EXACTLY this interface, because subphase 0.3 will replace the stub implementation behind it: export type WorkspaceRole = 'OWNER' | 'EDITOR' | 'READER'; export interface WorkspaceContextValue { workspaceId: string; workspaceSlug: string; workspaceName: string; role: WorkspaceRole; userId: string; userName: string | null; } export function WorkspaceProvider(props: { value: WorkspaceContextValue | null; children: React.ReactNode }); export function useWorkspace(): WorkspaceContextValue (throws outside a provider with a value); export function useOptionalWorkspace(): WorkspaceContextValue | null. The shell components consume useOptionalWorkspace and render a signed-out-safe state when it is null.
5. The app shell: AppShell with sidebar nav (Books and Settings entries, pointing at placeholder pages), top chrome, theme toggle, and the command palette shell with no entity search yet.
6. /dev/kitchen-sink renders every lifted primitive and returns 404 in production builds (NODE_ENV=production) — test that.
7. Lift generic guard tests that protect these primitives (for example token/colour discipline, no raw hex colours in components, no hand-rolled overlays) only if they are generic; skip compliance-specific ratchets.
8. Keep the dependency additions to what the lifted code imports.

lenses.name: ui-integration
lenses.focus: Do the lifted components actually render: imports resolve, tokens and styles present, dark mode works, no hydration errors on /dev/kitchen-sink in a production-mode dev or start (you may read build output but do not run the build yourself), WorkspaceContext matches the exact interface in the brief.

lenses.name: client-boundary
lenses.focus: No server-only module (src/env.ts, Prisma, node built-ins) imported from a 'use client' file directly or transitively; no next-intl server API used in client components; packages/ui imports nothing from @/.

0.1.title: Repository bootstrap
0.1.brief:
Roadmap prompt (docs/ROADMAP.md, Phase 0.1):
Create the Inkquisitor application skeleton: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, Prisma 7 with a multi-file schema folder, Jest 30 and Playwright, ESLint 9 flat config. Match the versions in inflect-compliance/package.json. Copy docker-compose.yml (Postgres with pgvector, PgBouncer, Redis, ClamAV) and the Dockerfile pattern. Add src/env.ts using @t3-oss/env-nextjs with only the variables this skeleton reads, and a separate src/env-client.ts for NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables. Create docs/carve-manifest.md with a table (Inkquisitor path, source path, source commit, edits made) and record every file you copy. Write CLAUDE.md stating the layer structure (app/api -> usecases -> policies -> repositories) and the nine rules in docs/ROADMAP.md section 3. Do not copy any compliance domain code.

Additional items for this subphase (owner decisions of 2026-11-18):
1. LICENSE: BUSL-1.1 mirroring /home/user/inflect-compliance/LICENSE exactly in its Terms and structure, with these Parameters: Licensor 'Inflect Ltd., a company registered in Bulgaria.'; Licensed Work 'Inkquisitor, as made available in this repository (github.com/RodnaPamet/Inkquisitor) and in each version released by the Licensor. The Licensed Work is (c) 2026 Inflect Ltd.' (use the copyright sign); Additional Use Grant: production use is permitted, provided that you may not use the Licensed Work to provide, to third parties, a hosted, managed, embedded, or software-as-a-service product or service (including any book-development, manuscript, story-planning, writing-assistant or author-interview product or service) that competes with any product or service offered by the Licensor; using it for your own writing, or your own organization's internal editorial work, is permitted. Change Date 2030-11-18 (four years after the initial version's first public availability; determined separately per version, as in inflect's wording). Change License Apache License, Version 2.0. Keep the same alternative-licensing contact line as inflect's LICENSE.
2. LICENSING.md explaining the licence in plain words (model it on inflect-compliance/LICENSING.md), stating that code derived from inflect-compliance is relicensed into Inkquisitor by the same licensor, and that the third-party designs ported later (MIT/Apache) are credited in NOTICE.
3. NOTICE: copyright line, the derivation from inflect-compliance at the recorded commit, and a section for third-party attributions (empty headings are fine for now).
4. package.json: name inkquisitor, private, license BUSL-1.1, engines node >=24 <25 (match inflect), a workspaces field only if you actually create a workspace package (0.2 will add packages/ui).
5. docs/ROADMAP.md: record the decisions as taken in section 2 (add a Status column: D1 decided: tldraw pinned to 3.x, commercial use with the watermark on, no licence key; D2 decided: BUSL-1.1, Inflect Ltd., mirrors inflect; D3, D4, D6 decided as the recommended defaults; D5 default assumed). Update hazard 1 and hazard 2 in section 1.3 accordingly, and rewrite the last two sentences of the Phase 3.1 prompt so that instead of a licence key it keeps tldraw pinned to 3.x with the watermark on and adds a guard test that fails if tldraw's major version moves. Change nothing else in the roadmap.
6. A minimal app: a home page that renders the product name and a one-line description, a /api/health route returning {status:'ok'}, a root layout. Tailwind 4 working (one utility class visibly applied).
7. Minimal CI at .github/workflows/ci.yml, triggered on pull_request and push to main, Node 24, npm ci with cache, concurrency group cancelling superseded runs, jobs named exactly: Lint, Typecheck, Test, Build. Test runs unit tests (and starts a postgres:16 service for later integration tests). Build must succeed in CI without secrets (use SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION or safe build-time defaults, never real secrets). Subphase 0.4 extends this file.
8. Scripts: dev, build, start, lint, typecheck, test (unit), test:integration (jest project for tests/integration, may have a placeholder-free empty project or a real smoke test against Postgres), test:e2e, db:generate, db:migrate. Jest config with separate unit and integration projects; SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 in jest setup.
9. .gitignore, .nvmrc or .node-version (24), .env.example listing every variable src/env.ts reads.
10. A short README.md: what Inkquisitor is (one paragraph from the roadmap intro), how to run it locally, link to docs/ROADMAP.md.
Keep the dependency set minimal for this subphase: only what the skeleton uses. Later subphases add their own dependencies.

lenses.name: ci-on-github
lenses.focus: Will .github/workflows/ci.yml actually pass on a fresh GitHub runner: npm ci against the committed lockfile, Node 24, Prisma client generation before typecheck/test/build, env needed at build time without secrets, job names exactly Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build, no step depending on local state. Also: is package-lock.json present and consistent with package.json (npm ci would fail otherwise)?

lenses.name: license-and-docs
lenses.focus: Is LICENSE a faithful BUSL-1.1 mirror of inflect-compliance's LICENSE with exactly the parameters in the brief (licensor, licensed work, additional use grant scope, change date 2030-11-18, Apache-2.0)? Are LICENSING.md, NOTICE, README, CLAUDE.md accurate and free of claims that are not true of the code? Were the ROADMAP.md edits limited to what the brief allows?
